item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Fri Oct 9 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Vespers at the Urban Well — Sun Oct 11, 5:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Vespers, Sunday evenings at 5:00 PM | In person only A contemplative candlelit service to nurture mind, body and spirit Join us Sunday evenings for Vespers, a warm and inviting weekly gathering in the serene surroundings of the Saint James Chapel. This quiet, reflective service embraces Christianity’s rich prayer traditions and the embodied practices that nurture our spiritual lives today. Gather with us for uplifting singing, find solace in moments of silence, and choose the posture that feels most comfortable as we open our hearts to listen for God’s voice and center ourselves for the week ahead. We have meditation cushions and chairs available for your comfort. We’ll celebrate Holy Communion on the third Sunday of the month. In person only. Everyone is welcome—come as you are!
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Oct 11, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Oct 14, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: A Century of Winnie-the-Pooh — Mon Dec 7, 5:00 PM — Lancaster
item.description:
Community, Presentation, Everyone
Winnie-the-Pooh is celebrating its 100th birthday this year! The stories A.A. Milne created have become classics that are as beloved now as they were when they were first published in October 1926. In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart
Source: Lancaster Libraries

item.title: Breakfast with Santa & Holiday Bazaar — Sat Dec 12, 8:45 AM — Church of the Apostles UCC
item.description:
Church of the Apostles and the American Cancer Society Relay for Life are teaming up for a festive morning of Breakfast with Santa and a Holiday Bazaar on Saturday, December 12! We’re making this year’s event bigger and better, with kids’ crafts and fun games provided by COA while parents browse a variety of local vendors throughout Fellowship Hall and our West Wing Lobby. And, of course, Santa will make his grand arrival by fire truck at 9 AM! 🚒🎅 Doors open at 8:45 AM. Breakfast will be served by wonderful American Cancer Society volunteers from 9–11 AM, with photos with Santa, crafts, raffles, and the Holiday Bazaar continuing until noon. Breakfast: • Adults and ages 13+: $12 • Children ages 2–12: $7 • Children under 2: Free The Holiday Bazaar is free to attend, and breakfast proceeds benefit the American Cancer Society Relay for Life of Lancaster County. Come hungry, bring the kids, and get your holiday season started with a morning of food, fun, shopping, and Santa! 🎄

item.title: Sparkdate: Tellus AfterDark — Tue Oct 6, 6:30 PM — Tellus360
item.description:
A downtown Lancaster staple with a rooftop that turns any night into something worth dressing up for. Open sky, string lights, and a bar that’s easy to linger at — the kind of place that does half the work of making people comfortable before anyone even says hello. Add real conversations instead of small talk that goes nowhere, and you’ve got a night built for singles who actually want to meet someone, not just match with them.
How the night works:Check in with a host and get a name tag — there’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements:First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play — that’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. item.title: Redemption Time — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Join us at the Ware Center for a free screening of the film Redemption Time—plus a community discussion panel and a Q&A with the filmmakers. Witness a powerful multimedia performance film featuring poet Jimmy Santiago Baca and jazz violinist Christian Howes, two formerly incarcerated artists who reclaimed their lives through art. Combining spoken word, music, and visual art, Redemption Time invites audiences into a shared space of healing and transformation.
Come early for a pre-show community panel at 6:15 pm, and stay after the film for a post-screening Q&A with Dr. David Gonzalez, director of Redemption Time, and Christian Howes, a formerly incarcerated individual featured in Redemption Time and an award-winning jazz violinist. Admission is free! Tickets are required for entry.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Revolution to Reconstruction with Clint Smith — Wed Oct 7, 5:00 PM — LancasterHistory
item.description:
LancasterHistory will welcome award-winning author Clint Smith to the Ware Center for Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality. Smith, author of How the Word Is Passed and Above Ground, will explore Pennsylvania’s central role in shaping our nation’s evolving ideals of liberty and equality. The event will include a lecture followed by Q&A. Pocket Books will also be on site selling signed copies of How the word is passed. The lecture is FREE, but advance registration is required and space is limited.
